topics.topic: India’s Resilient Production Systems in Agriculture
topics.why_in_news: PIB highlighted India’s efforts to strengthen climate-resilient agricultural production systems through technology adoption, sustainable farming and food security measures.
prelims_quick_notes: Focus on climate-resilient agriculture and sustainable food systems.
Promotes diversification, water efficiency and soil health management.
Encourages use of climate-smart farming practices.
Supports food security amid climate change challenges.
Includes technology integration and precision agriculture.
Promotes crop insurance and risk reduction mechanisms.
Linked with sustainable agriculture and rural livelihoods.
Supports long-term productivity and resilience.
important_facts: Agriculture remains major livelihood source in India.
Climate change affects rainfall, crop productivity and water availability.
Sustainable agriculture linked with SDG-2 (Zero Hunger).
exam_relevance: Important for Agriculture, Economy and Environment.
Useful for food security, climate resilience and rural economy topics.
Can be linked with sustainable development and farmer welfare.
prelims_traps: Climate-resilient agriculture is not limited to irrigation alone.
Food security includes availability, access and affordability.
Millets require comparatively lower water than many major crops.

topics.topic: Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) Annual Report 2025
topics.why_in_news: Government released Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) Annual Report 2025 highlighting improvements in labour participation, employment trends and workforce formalisation in India.
prelims_quick_notes: PLFS conducted by National Statistical Office (NSO).
Provides official estimates on employment and unemployment.
Measures Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR) and Unemployment Rate (UR).
PLFS shifted to calendar year format (January–December) from 2025.
Useful for labour market reforms and employment policy analysis.
Covers both rural and urban employment trends.
Supports evidence-based policymaking and workforce planning.
Important for analysing demographic dividend and labour formalisation.
key_findings_and_indicators: LFPR increased indicating greater participation in labour market.
WPR improved reflecting rise in employment levels.
Unemployment Rate declined compared to previous years.
Female labour force participation showed improvement.
Rural labour participation remained higher than urban areas.
Formalisation trends improved through EPFO and ESIC expansion.
Employment growth linked with services, construction and manufacturing sectors.
Survey sample size increased significantly in redesigned PLFS.
important_facts: NSO functions under Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).
LFPR includes employed and unemployed persons seeking work.
UR excludes persons not willing to work.
PLFS provides both rural and urban labour market estimates.
PLFS sample size increased around 2.65 times in redesigned survey.
Useful for employment, skilling and labour policy formulation.
exam_relevance: Important for Economy, Employment and Inclusive Growth.
Useful for labour reforms, skilling and demographic dividend topics.
Can be linked with formalisation, urbanisation and economic growth.
prelims_traps: LFPR and WPR are not the same indicators.
Unemployment Rate includes only active labour force participants.
PLFS is conducted by NSO under MoSPI, not RBI.
LFPR includes both employed and unemployed persons seeking work.

prelims_traps.topic: Key Labour Market Indicators in India
prelims_traps.why_in_news: PLFS Annual Report 2025 highlighted major labour market indicators reflecting employment trends, workforce participation and changing structure of India’s economy.
prelims_quick_notes: LFPR measures proportion of population participating in labour force.
WPR measures proportion of employed persons in population.
UR measures percentage of unemployed persons within labour force.
Female Labour Force Participation Rate showed improvement.
Rural labour participation generally higher than urban areas.
Services sector remains major employment generator.
Formalisation linked with EPFO and ESIC expansion.
Labour indicators help assess economic and social development.
key_findings_and_indicators: LFPR increased indicating improved labour market participation.
WPR improved reflecting rise in employment opportunities.
Unemployment Rate declined compared to previous survey cycles.
Urban unemployment remained relatively higher than rural areas.
Self-employment continues to form major employment category.
Construction and services sectors contributed strongly to employment generation.
Formal employment trends strengthened through digital and policy reforms.
important_facts: LFPR includes employed and unemployed persons seeking work.
UR excludes persons outside labour force.
PLFS conducted by NSO under MoSPI.
Survey useful for labour policy and economic planning.
PLFS provides both rural and urban labour statistics.
exam_relevance: Important for Economy, Employment and Human Capital.
Useful for labour reforms, demographic dividend and inclusive growth.
Can be linked with skilling, urbanisation and formalisation.
prelims_traps: LFPR and WPR are conceptually different indicators.
UR is calculated within labour force, not total population.
Higher LFPR does not automatically mean lower unemployment.
